claim: Let \(P_6\) be the path graph on six vertices and let \(P_6\times P_6\) denote the categorical graph product. Then its matching complex satisfies \(\mathsf{M}(P_6\times P_6)\simeq\bigvee^{169}S^{11}\). More precisely, \(P_6\times P_6\) is the disjoint union of two isomorphic connected components \(C\), each with 18 vertices and 25 edges, and \(\mathsf{M}(C)\simeq\bigvee^{13}S^5\); the join decomposition of the matching complex therefore gives the stated wedge of 169 eleven-spheres.

correctness.rationale: The exact graph definition is reconstructed from scratch. The verifier proves the parity decomposition into two connected isomorphic 18-vertex, 25-edge components; exhaustively enumerates all 12,900 nonempty matching faces of one component; checks all 63,027 Hasse covers; and verifies a 6,443-pair acyclic matching leaving exactly one critical \(0\)-cell and thirteen critical \(5\)-cells. This gives \(\mathsf{M}(C)\simeq\bigvee^{13}S^5\). The disjoint-union matching complex is the join of the two component complexes, yielding \(\bigvee^{169}S^{11}\). Independent mod-\(2\) boundary ranks give reduced Betti rank 13 only in degree \(5\), consistent with the Morse result. No infinite conclusion is inferred from the finite computation.

value.rationale: The parameter pair \((6,6)\) is the first genuinely new unordered pair beyond the proved small-width range, so it is a natural boundary test of Conjecture 6.2 rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
